summary: In a major operational milestone for defense integration, the U.S. Army welcomed its first 600 enlisted space soldiers, while aerospace contractor Boeing secured a potential $14.7 billion PAC-3 seeker contract. In international commercial space developments, Nebex partnered with Thrusters Unlimited in a deal aimed at unlocking $700 million for Mexico’s space ecosystem, even as resource competition intensifies across the sector due to a surge in megaconstellations. To accommodate expanding operational requirements, Vandenberg is evaluating new launch support facilities and possible on-site manufacturing. On the flight test and defense technology front, Northrop Grumman conducted the first flight of its self-funded Talon Blue Collaborative Combat Aircraft, and the Pentagon selected four vendors for a counter-drone directed energy pilot program. In civil space management, NASA published its FY26 performance expectations and standards. In scientific research, engineers used X-rays and artificial intelligence to analyze spacecraft heat shields burning in real time, while astronomers relying on the Hubble Space Telescope resolved a long-standing cold case by identifying a suspected second-generation planet. Readers should watch next for NASA's live coverage of the upcoming SpaceX Crew-12 return and splashdown.
